title: Assistance that keeps engineering judgment visible
description: AIFIELD explores command-line and Model Context Protocol workflows for proposed design actions. A human reviews and applies changes, and the supplied material does not support a claim of fully autonomous chip design.
lead: AIFIELD explores command-line and Model Context Protocol workflows for proposed design actions. A human reviews and applies changes, and the supplied material does not support a claim of fully autonomous chip design.

sections.heading: A bounded workflow
body: An assistant can receive a design question, inspect available context and propose a command or change. The engineer evaluates assumptions, chooses whether to apply it and checks the resulting simulation. Proposed output is not accepted design evidence until reviewed.

sections.heading: Tool and data boundaries
body: Some solver work is described as local. The treatment of context sent to any external assistant needs a precise deployment-specific account before confidentiality statements can be made. This page makes no promise that all design data stays local.

sections.heading: What needs evaluation
body: A useful assessment would track task completion, erroneous proposals, required human corrections and repeatability on documented examples. The next milestone is to specify supported actions and measure the assistance against a manual baseline.
